objective: Refuse a scenario manifest whose fault_type is not a declared fault, so an undeclared or misspelled name cannot execute as a fault-free control and be reported as confirmed.
decision_supported: Whether the declared fault_type domain is closed at manifest admission, and whether it is pinned in the scenario schema as well as in the Pydantic model.
acceptance: an undeclared fault_type is refused by validate_simulation_manifest with the accepted set named
an undeclared fault_type is refused by load_scenario_manifests, so the runner cannot start a run with it
every declared fault and the none control are still accepted
the scenario schema enum and the Python declared set agree, and a test asserts it
evidence: the typo manifest camera_droput was refused with 'unsupported fault_type' instead of reporting confirmed
validate_scenarios.py: 12 frozen and 24 expanded manifests pass
stop_conditions: a committed manifest uses a fault name outside the declared set
closing the domain would require changing the frozen scenario distribution
the schema enum and the model cannot be kept in one place
risks_and_fallbacks: Closing the domain is reject-only for the 36 committed manifests, which were checked first.
A future fault name must extend FaultType and the schema together in one change.
Fallback if the enum cannot be kept in one place: keep the schema permissive and rely on the model check, and record that divergence here.
